summary: Rodanthe station of the US Life-Saving Service, commissioned in 1874; in 1918 its crew saved 42 sailors from the torpedoed tanker Mirlo. Now a museum.

access.note: Museum run by the Chicamacomico Historical Association, 23645 N.C. Highway 12, Rodanthe; the association's page mentions admission fees, so check current hours and prices.

events.note: Station house built under D. Simpson's contract (23 April 1874); commissioned 4 December 1874
L. B. (Little Banister) Midgett succeeds Pugh
Josiah Wescott replaces Midgett (association: Midgett ill)
Samuel W. Tilton, 17 February; George L. Fessenden, 27 April
Hurricane of mid-August: tide round the station, boathouse moved 30 ft; Minnie Bergen crew landed 18 August
All 35 of the British ship Clyde landed by breeches buoy, 9 March
New station house completed (under construction 1910) to replace a worn-out building
Life-Saving Service merged into the Coast Guard (January 1915); John Allen Midgett Jr. appointed captain (keeper)
1874 house rolled 960 yards to stand abreast of the 1911 station (22 April to about 22 May)
Decommissioned as a Coast Guard station in May
Deeded to Mrs. Lurania Midgett, 5 December; buildings disposed of by GSA in 1968
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, 12 December (ref. 76000164)

keepers.name: Benjamin S. Pugh
keepers.note: First keeper, commissioned 4 Dec 1874 as 'Benjamin Pugh' (association). The 1876 report's keeper column reads 'Benjamin 8. Pugh' in the OCR; the page image (printed p. 18, District No. 6) shows the row 'No. 9 Chicamicomico ... Benjamin S. Pugh'. Appointed keeper of another station in 1879 (not named).

keepers.name: L. B. Midgett
keepers.note: Little Banister 'Capt. Ban' Midgett (association: 'III'); 'Keeper Midgett' of Station No. 18 in the 1882 report (Oct 1881); 'L. B. Midgett, keeper of the Chicamicomico Station' in the 1884 report; an 1884 testimonial is addressed to 'L. B. Midgett, Jr.'. Replaced in 1888 by Wescott, ill (association).

keepers.name: Josiah H. Wescott
keepers.note: Also Westcott, J. H. Wescott. Named as Chicamacomico keeper in March 1891, March 1892 and October 1893; keeper of New Inlet by June 1894. The 1904 end date for New Inlet rests on the order of names in a letter addressed to Keepers Westcott and Midgett of the New Inlet and Chicamacomico stations.

keepers.name: L. Banister Midgett
keepers.note: Same man as L. B. Midgett above (association: resumed in 1894 after illness). Keeper in April 1898 (Fessenden report); named by order in a 1904 letter to the keepers of New Inlet and Chicamacomico; addressed outright as 'Keeper Chicamacomico Life-Saving Station' in 1906; last named as 'Keeper Midgett, at Chicamacomico' for October 1907. End of tenure and successor before 1915 not found.

keepers.name: John Allen Midgett Jr.
keepers.note: Called Captain and Keeper in the sources; Coast Guard from 1915. Led the Mirlo rescue, 16 August 1918. Sources disagree on his death: December 1938 (association) or 9 February 1938 (Wikipedia, citing the Dictionary of North Carolina Biography).

keepers.name: Levene Midgett
keepers.note: Captain of the station until it was decommissioned in 1954 (association: took over December 1938).

keepers.name: Benjamin O'Neal
keepers.note: Substitute for the No. 1 surfman, who was home sick; found the Thomas J. Lancaster, October 1881.

keepers.name: Stanley Midgett
keepers.note: Volunteer who had been hauling wood to the station; went with the crew to the Thomas J. Lancaster, October 1881.

keepers.name: E. S. Midgett
keepers.note: Discovered the schooner George L. Fessenden on 26 April 1898.

keepers.name: C. P. Midgett
keepers.note: Neighbourhood volunteer at the wreck of the George L. Fessenden, April 1898.

keepers.name: A. F. Midgett

keepers.name: Arthur V. Midgett

keepers.name: Prochorus L. O'Neal
keepers.note: Surfman No. 5 ('P. L. O'Neal' in the log); honoured for the Mirlo rescue.

keepers.name: Clarence E. Midgett

wrecks.outcome: Philadelphia ice schooner, 13 aboard; stranded 3.5 miles north of the station; six survivors landed by surfboat the next morning, one a child who died that night at the station
Water-logged schooner beached on purpose; all five aboard landed by breeches buoy
British steamer ashore in fog a mile and a quarter south of the station; 19 of 26 lost, 7 saved
British barkentine stranded about noon; crew landed in about thirty minutes
Four-masted schooner stranded on the outer bar; crew and managing owner dealt with by the Chicamacomico crew and neighbouring stations (the master's letter praises the life car)
Schooner broke up 250 yards off the beach; 3 of 7 saved
Schooner destroyed 2.5 miles below Gull Shoal station in the West Indian hurricane; Chicamacomico, Little Kinnakeet and Gull Shoal crews assembled; three men taken from the surf, five aboard died
Leaking schooner let drift onto the beach; crew of seven landed by breeches buoy
British ship ashore; all 35 aboard landed by breeches buoy
British tanker torpedoed by U-117; 42 of 51 saved by the station's motor surfboat

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and Wikipedia give 1874, the year the first station house was built and commissioned (4 Dec 1874). A second station house was completed in 1911; the 1874 house became the boathouse and was moved in 1918. Both survive.

notes_for_editor: Gaps and cautions. (1) The NRHP nomination (76000164) is 'not yet digitized' on NPGallery, so the chronology rests on the association's history pages (modern, from station records), the USLSS Heritage Association, and the Life-Saving Service annual reports 1876-1908. The 1910-1914 LSS reports are not in the corpus, so the 1911 building has no primary source here and no architect is named (a search-result snippet from an NCSU/SHPO photo caption says Mendeleff designed it; unverified, the page returned 503). (2) Keepers: Pugh 1874-79 and Midgett from 1879 come from the association's page. The 1876 report's keeper column was matched to the station by column order (Pugh is the 9th name and Chicamicomico the 9th locality); the fact-check read the page image (printed p. 18), where the row is plain, and it agrees with the association. The same page puts an 'L. B. Midgett' at Little Kinnakeet in 1876; that is only an initials match to Chicamacomico's L. B. Midgett, so it was removed from other_stations (never infer a person from a shared name) and is left here for a human to confirm. (3) The Midgett/Wescott exchange is documented by the LSS reports: Wescott at Chicamacomico in 1891, 1892 and October 1893 and Midgett at New Inlet in 1891 and 1893; Wescott at New Inlet by June 1894 and in 1904; Midgett at Chicamacomico in 1898, 1904, 1906 and 1907. The association explains 1888 as Midgett's illness, but the reports show him keeping New Inlet, so 'ill' may not be the whole story. (4) Suffix conflict: the association calls L. B. Midgett 'III'; an 1884 testimonial is addressed to 'L. B. Midgett, Jr.'. (5) No keeper is named for 1908-1915 in the sources read; John Allen Midgett Jr.'s 1915 appointment is the association's (Wikipedia says he enlisted in 1898 and commanded a station when the services merged). His death is 9 Feb 1938 (Wikipedia, citing Powell) or December 1938 (association). The 'ex-keeper John Allen Midgett' whose house was used in 1891 may be his father; the sources do not say, so he is not on the roster. (6) Minnie Bergen: the 1900 report's entry (p. 86) is a multi-column table whose texts were matched to Chicamacomico by their order; it agrees with the master's letter (p. 205, written at Chicamacomico, breeches buoy, 18 August) and with the benefaction list (seven men); the fact-check read the page images for pp. 86, 57 and 205 and the row for 18 August plainly reads 'Am. sc. Minnie Bergen | Chicamacomico, North Carolina'. (7) Honours for the Mirlo crew: the association says British gold medals and the Board of Trade cup on 8 Nov 1921 and Grand Crosses on 23 July 1930; Wikipedia says cup 1918 and a US Gold Lifesaving Medal six years later; unresolved. The association's account puts the torpedoing at 4.40 p.m.; Midgett's 1918 report in the newspaper says 4:30. (8) The two 1918 newspaper pages (Lancaster News, Detroiter Abend-Post) have poor OCR; the Lancaster headline is partly illegible and its station number garbled. They were the only Chronicling America hits from one search (the loc.gov queue was congested). (9) No photographs were collected. The record's coordinates (35.595, -75.465) agree with the Service's 1879 position (35 35 30 N, 75 27 30 W); the record's status_note about unusable positions looks like a template. (10) The USLSS Heritage Association's note on the 1967 deed and 1968 GSA disposal says it comes from the Coast Guard Historian's site, which this project may not use; it is cited here as the Heritage Association's page and should be checked against a primary record. (11) Fact-check 2026-10-21: all 202 original evidence quotes were found in the cached sources on the first run; the checks that mattered were meaning, attribution and wording.
